theory.mode: Symmetric scale - no traditional modes. Only 2 possible whole tone scales exist (C and C#/D♭). Every note can function as the root, producing the same interval structure.

relativeScale.name: No traditional relative scale
relativeScale.intervalDistance: Any whole tone scale member can serve as root; C Whole Tone and D♭ Whole Tone are the only two distinct collections

keyExamples.notes: C - D - E - F# - G# - A# - C
keyExamples.commonUse: Most common starting point for whole tone study, easy to visualize, Debussy's primary whole tone collection

keyExamples.notes: G - A - B - C# - D# - F - G
keyExamples.commonUse: Guitar-friendly key, belongs to the same whole tone collection as C Whole Tone

keyExamples.notes: D - E - F# - G# - A# - C - D
keyExamples.commonUse: Same collection as C Whole Tone starting from D, comfortable for guitar open-string root

keyExamples.notes: A - B - C# - D# - F - G - A
keyExamples.commonUse: Open string root on guitar, same collection as C Whole Tone, good for jazz augmented chord voicings

patterns.position: Open Position (C Whole Tone, starting 3rd fret 5th string)
patterns.description: Symmetrical fingering pattern starting from C on the 5th string. Every interval is a whole step, creating an unusually regular and uniform fretboard shape.
Moveable whole tone pattern starting from A on the 6th string 5th fret. The symmetric nature means this pattern repeats every whole step.
Upper register whole tone pattern for ethereal, floating melodic lines. Useful for creating impressionistic textures in higher registers.

commonPositions.usage: Impressionistic passages, augmented chord contexts, whole tone introduction
Jazz soloing over augmented and dominant 7#5 chords
Higher register floating lines, film score textures, ambient playing

diatonicChords.function: Tonic - All triads built on whole tone scale degrees are augmented; no major or minor triads exist
Supertonic - Same augmented quality, enharmonically equivalent to Caug inversion
Mediant - Enharmonic equivalent of Caug (E - G# - B#/C)
Augmented fourth degree - Enharmonically equivalent to Daug inversion
Augmented fifth degree - Enharmonically equivalent to Caug inversion
Subtonic - Enharmonically equivalent to Daug inversion. Only 2 unique augmented triads exist in each whole tone scale.

commonProgressions.name: Augmented Drift (Caug - Daug - Eaug)
commonProgressions.description: Parallel augmented chord movement creating a floating, directionless quality. Each chord dissolves into the next with no strong resolution.

commonProgressions.name: Dominant Augmented Resolution (C7#5 - Fmaj7)
commonProgressions.description: Whole tone scale applied over a dominant 7#5 chord resolving to a major chord. The most common practical application in jazz harmony.

commonProgressions.name: Impressionist Color Shift (Caug - D♭aug - Caug)
commonProgressions.description: Shifting between the two whole tone collections creates a shimmering, color-change effect used in impressionist and film music.

genreApplications.usage: Foundational scale for impressionist composition, creating dreamlike atmospheres without strong tonal gravity
Applied over augmented chords and dominant 7#5 chords for altered, floating improvisation with no tonal center
examples: Thelonious Monk - whole tone runs in improvisations
Wayne Shorter - whole tone passages in compositions

genreApplications.usage: Creates dreamlike, surreal, and disorienting atmospheres for dream sequences, underwater scenes, and transitions

famousSongs.title: Voiles (Preludes Book 1)
famousSongs.usage: Almost entirely based on the whole tone scale, the definitive whole tone composition in Western music
famousSongs.learningValue: The quintessential whole tone composition, demonstrates pure whole tone harmony and melody

famousSongs.title: You Are the Sunshine of My Life
famousSongs.usage: Introduction uses whole tone ascending movement to create a dreamy, magical opening
famousSongs.learningValue: Shows whole tone scale used as a brief color effect in popular music

famousSongs.title: Falling Grace
famousSongs.usage: Whole tone passages woven through jazz harmonic changes, demonstrating the scale's jazz vocabulary potential
famousSongs.learningValue: Demonstrates how whole tone fragments integrate into modern jazz lines

famousSongs.title: Four on Six
famousSongs.usage: Whole tone runs used over dominant chords as a tension device before resolving to tonal centers
famousSongs.learningValue: Shows how jazz masters use whole tone as a momentary color over dominant chords

famousSongs.title: L'isle joyeuse
famousSongs.usage: Extended whole tone passages creating shimmering, dreamlike textures within a larger tonal framework
famousSongs.learningValue: Advanced impressionist application of whole tone scale integrated with tonal writing

practiceExercises.name: C Whole Tone Scale Runs
practiceExercises.description: Practice the C whole tone scale ascending and descending, internalizing the uniform whole-step interval and the symmetrical fingering pattern
instructions: Play C whole tone ascending and descending with even rhythm, noting how each step is exactly a whole tone
Practice in two adjacent positions to cover both whole tone collections (C and D♭)
Close your eyes and focus on the floating, directionless quality of the scale's sound

practiceExercises.name: Augmented Arpeggio Patterns
practiceExercises.description: Practice augmented triads built on each scale degree to hear how the whole tone scale generates only augmented harmony
instructions: Play Caug, Daug, Eaug arpeggios ascending through the scale, noting they are all inversions of two triads
Connect the arpeggios into flowing lines that outline the whole tone harmony
Apply over a C7#5 backing chord to hear the augmented dominant context

practiceExercises.name: Dominant 7#5 Application
practiceExercises.description: Apply the whole tone scale over a dominant 7#5 chord resolving to a major chord, the most practical jazz application
instructions: Practice over a C7#5 to Fmaj7 vamp, using whole tone scale over the dominant chord
Focus on creating tension with the whole tone scale and resolving smoothly to a chord tone of the target major chord
Experiment with different rhythmic groupings to avoid the scale sounding like a simple exercise

relatedScales.differences: Lydian Dominant (melodic minor mode 4) has a perfect 5th; whole tone has augmented 5th and one fewer note
relatedScales.usage: Lydian Dominant adds more tonal stability; whole tone is fully floating and symmetric

relatedScales.differences: Augmented scale alternates minor 3rds and half steps (C-E♭-E-G-A♭-B); whole tone uses all whole steps
relatedScales.usage: Augmented scale has more tonal grounding; whole tone is completely uniform and directionless

relatedScales.relationship: Contains all notes of both whole tone collections
relatedScales.differences: Chromatic has all 12 semitones; whole tone selects every other note (6 notes) from the chromatic scale
relatedScales.usage: Chromatic is used for pure passing-tone movement; whole tone creates a specific augmented color

prerequisites: Major scale and basic mode knowledge
Familiarity with augmented triads and dominant 7th chords
nextSteps: Diminished (octatonic) scale as another symmetric scale
Lydian Dominant mode for dominant chord applications with more tonal context

exercises: Augmented arpeggio patterns across the fretboard

practiceRoutine.focus: Musical application in jazz and creative composition
exercises: Improvise over V7#5-I resolutions in jazz standards
Create dreamy and impressionistic musical phrases
